before_review.assessment: SOURCE panels show one elongated building: a recessed concrete frame, a timber upper hall beneath a sagging roof, a projecting glazed perimeter, and stacked ramps at one short end. Exterior views share the ramp and roof landmarks; interior views, sections and plans show cellular lower rooms, a substantial double-height space, spiral circulation and guarded circular floor openings. The exploded diagram confirms the layered assembly. CURRENT captures the principal exterior arrangement, but the interior remains substantially more open, receiving landings meet uninterrupted glazing, and several upper-floor holes lack guards. Geographic orientation and exact dimensions are not established by the source images; the uncut CURRENT views cannot verify every internal connection.

issues.problem: SOURCE plans and sections show enclosed lower-storey rooms and an asymmetric double-height interior. CURRENT views 15–17 and 23–25 expose largely uninterrupted floor plates and bare columns, omitting major internal spatial boundaries.
issues.action: Locally add the source-visible room enclosures and correct the corresponding floor opening for the double-height space. Retain correctly positioned structural members; use the source plans and sections together to locate these patches.

issues.problem: CURRENT views 23–26 show continuous glass panels and framing across the apparent receiving passages. Openings in the landing rails therefore do not establish usable connections through the envelope. SOURCE plans show circulation connecting perimeter access with interior door openings.
issues.action: At each receiving passage, provide an actual opening or operable door through the glazing, aligned with the landing and interior access. Resolve any brace crossing that passage locally, preserving adjacent glazing.

issues.problem: SOURCE interior panel 4 shows circular floor openings enclosed by raised mesh guards. CURRENT view 18 shows the foreground and middle circular holes with exposed, unguarded edges; only the distant stair opening has a guard.
issues.action: Add circular mesh guards around the exposed openings, joined to the floor perimeter, matching the source’s slender posts and raised top rail.

keep: Short-end roof profile with a central sag and unequal raised edges.
Recessed lower concrete column line beneath the projecting perimeter.
Three stacked inclined ramp runs at the short end.

after_review.assessment: SOURCE panels show one elongated building: a retained concrete frame with split-level/double-height spaces, a glazed upper timber hall beneath a concave roof, projecting circulation decks, end ramps, spiral stairs and circular floor openings. Exterior perspectives share the ramp end and adjoining long facade; interior panels show the upper hall and lower double-height workspace; sections, plans and exploded diagrams establish their relationships. CURRENT captures the broad roof profile and circulation concept, but differs in ramp placement, internal floor continuity and opening guards. Absolute dimensions are unconfirmed. Uncut section views and roof-occluded plans cannot establish concealed connections or partition fidelity.

issues.problem: CURRENT places all three diagonal ramp flights prominently outside the end glazing, with large projecting turnaround platforms. SOURCE 1–2 show the upper flights behind the outer glazed screen and a more restrained relationship between ramps, perimeter decks and end landings.
issues.action: Locally reposition the upper flights within the screened circulation zone and reduce the excessive landing projections. Align each flight endpoint with its receiving deck and opening; close-ups 24–26 still show railing across the apparent approach, so provide actual clear passages and connected landings.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 lower and sections 5/8 show a double-height hall beside an intermediate floor, with an open upper gallery and spiral connection. CURRENT 23 instead shows a continuous low ceiling across the hall, suppressing this major interior volume.
issues.action: Remove only the slab and beam portions spanning the source-backed void. Retain the adjacent intermediate floor and concrete columns, and connect the spiral stair to the resulting gallery edge.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 upper shows circular floor openings enclosed by substantial cylindrical mesh guards. CURRENT 18 leaves the foreground circular opening unguarded and uses sparse vertical bars around the larger stair opening.
issues.action: Add continuous circular mesh guards around the corresponding openings and revise the existing stair guard locally, preserving clear stair access.

keep: Concave transverse roof profile with unequal edge heights.
Raised timber hall set inward from the outer glazed perimeter.
Recurring rectangular concrete columns visible along the lower facade.

before_review.assessment: SOURCE 1–2 establish the ramp end and adjoining long facade: a rectangular concrete frame, projecting glazed buffer galleries, stacked ramps and a raised timber hall with a concave roof. SOURCE 3 shows the entrance and open-grid gallery undersides; SOURCE 4 shows the curved timber ceiling, guarded circular openings and a tall lower hall with a spiral stair. SOURCE 5–8 supply sections, structural layers and three floor plans, confirming partial intermediate floors and connected circulation. CURRENT retains these main exterior landmarks, but the lower hall’s vertical openness, stair assembly and gallery construction differ visibly. The uncut section views and roof-occluded plan cannot verify internal floor extents; exact dimensions and concealed joints remain uncertain.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 lower shows a tall hall beside a partial upper gallery; SOURCE 5, 7 and 8 confirm the corresponding floor void. CURRENT 23 instead shows a low ceiling of repeated beams across the hall, suppressing this defining double-height space.
issues.action: Locally trim the intermediate slab and associated beams to the source-backed void boundary, retaining the adjoining occupied floor and supporting columns.

issues.problem: The source spiral stair has a coherent helical flight, continuous curved guarding and a connected upper landing. CURRENT 23 shows separated tread sequences without a legible continuous supporting assembly or complete guarding; CURRENT 18 also shows an unguarded circular opening.
issues.action: Connect the existing stair flights to their floor openings and landings, complete the curved guards, and guard the exposed circular opening. Verify actual tread and landing connections rather than apparent overlap.

issues.problem: SOURCE 3 shows open-grid gallery decking on slender projecting beams, with light mesh guards. CURRENT 17 and 24–26 show broad opaque gallery soffits and coarse horizontal-bar guards, making the buffer galleries substantially heavier and less permeable.
issues.action: Patch the visible gallery decks to open grating with discrete supporting beams, and replace the coarse guard infill with the source’s fine mesh treatment while preserving aligned landing thresholds.

keep: Concave transverse profile of the raised hall roof, including its unequal edge heights.
Stacked ramp flights descending across the short end in the source’s observed direction.
Raised timber hall set inside the wider rectangular buffer-gallery footprint.

after_review.assessment: SOURCE panels show one elongated building: retained concrete framing, staggered interior floors and a double-height region, a glazed timber upper hall beneath a concave roof, and projecting perimeter circulation connected by end ramps. End views share the descending ramp landmark; obliques establish its connection to the long-side galleries. Interior panels show circular floor openings with mesh guards; plans and sections establish internal voids and rooms. CURRENT captures the principal roof profile and projecting circulation, but the close-ups show apparent glazing barriers at ramp returns, while guard construction differs visibly. Uncut section-position views and the roof-obscured plan cannot verify the internal floor arrangement. No numerical dimensions are user-confirmed here, and hidden connections remain uncertain.

issues.problem: The ramp-to-gallery routes appear closed by full-height glazed panels and continuous horizontal framing. Coplanar walking surfaces alone do not establish an open connection; SOURCE shows continuous circulation around these returns.
issues.action: Locally open the glazing at each landing connection, terminate crossing framing outside the passage, and retain flush ramp-to-gallery walking surfaces. Verify each junction from both sides.

issues.problem: CURRENT substitutes repeated open horizontal-bar guards for the fine mesh infill visible along SOURCE ramps and galleries. The stacked bars substantially change the circulation envelope’s appearance.
issues.action: Retain correctly positioned decks and posts; replace the intermediate horizontal-bar arrangement with fine mesh panels and slender perimeter rails where SOURCE shows them.

issues.problem: The foreground circular floor opening has no raised enclosure. SOURCE’s upper interior shows circular openings surrounded by cylindrical mesh guards.
issues.action: Add a fitted cylindrical mesh guard around the exposed opening, joined to the floor perimeter; preserve the existing opening rather than filling it.

keep: Concave transverse roof profile with unequal edge heights.
Recessed upper-hall glazing beneath the curved roof.
Descending end-ramp direction visible in the SOURCE end elevations.

before_review.assessment: SOURCE 1–2 establish the ramp end and adjoining long facade: a recessed building frame, three descending ramp flights, projecting galleries, a transparent upper enclosure and a raised concave timber roof. SOURCE 3 shows the glazed entrance and gallery underside; SOURCE 4 shows the curved timber ceiling, pale floor, curtain divisions and guarded circular openings. SOURCE 5 and 8 show stepped interior floor levels and substantial voids; SOURCE 6 separates the structural layers; all three SOURCE 7 plans show distinct floor arrangements. CURRENT captures the principal exterior composition, but its enclosure reads substantially heavier and its upper interior remains incomplete. The uncut section views and roof-occluded plan cannot establish whether the concealed floor arrangements match. No numerical dimensions were supplied, and screenshots alone cannot certify concealed joints.

issues.problem: CURRENT 16–17 substitutes prominent stacked rails and heavy framing for the source’s slender white enclosure and fine mesh gallery guards. This obscures the recessed glazing and overwhelms the otherwise comparable massing.
issues.action: Locally reduce the visible frame and rail sections, apply the source’s light finish, and replace coarse horizontal guard infill with fine mesh where shown. Preserve the gallery positions and ramp slopes.

issues.problem: CURRENT 18 shows circular floor openings without surrounding guards, while SOURCE 4 shows continuous cylindrical mesh protection. The existing guarded opening does not resolve the exposed openings elsewhere.
issues.action: Match the source-backed opening locations and fit continuous mesh guards around their exposed perimeters, seated on the floor and connected at their returns.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 shows a pale floor and large curved translucent curtain divisions beneath the timber ceiling. CURRENT 18 instead has an uninterrupted brown floor and lacks those prominent spatial divisions.
issues.action: Change the upper floor to the observed pale finish and add the visible curved curtain tracks and translucent hanging panels. Retain the concave timber ceiling.

keep: Concave roof end profile with its higher right edge in the matched ramp-end view.
Three descending ramp flights across the ramp end.
Open gallery underside with projecting transverse beams and recessed glazing.

after_review.assessment: SOURCE 1–2 show the same elongated building from the ramp end, adjoining long elevation and above: a recessed lower frame, projecting two-storey glazed buffer, zigzag ramps and a raised concave roof. SOURCE 3 shows entrance glazing and thin grating balconies with exposed supporting beams. SOURCE 4 shows the timber ceiling, circular guarded floor openings and a double-height interior with spiral stair. SOURCE 5–8 provide sections, plans and an exploded assembly confirming the layered frame, partial intermediate floor and lightweight outer enclosure. CURRENT reproduces the main arrangement, but adds conspicuous projecting landings, substitutes heavy open rails for fine mesh guards, and does not visibly resolve the circular floor openings. No numerical dimensions are supplied; roof-obscured plans and uncut exterior views cannot verify hidden floor layouts or structural joints.

issues.problem: CURRENT 15–16 show repeated balcony landing stubs extending beyond both sides of the glazed end enclosure at upper levels. SOURCE 1–2 show the upper circulation contained within the rectangular enclosure, with the lower open terrace and ground ramp distinguished below. These added projections change the end silhouette and circulation connections.
issues.action: Locally shorten the unsupported upper landing extensions to the source enclosure boundary; connect each ramp termination flush to its corresponding landing, retaining the source-backed lower terrace and ground approach.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 shows clear circular voids through the pale floor, enclosed by mesh guards. CURRENT 18 shows tan surfaces and straight floor edges continuing across the guarded circles, so the rings read as cages standing over covered or obstructed openings.
issues.action: Cut the circular openings through all overlapping floor faces and remove crossing infill within their footprints. Seat the guards continuously around the resulting slab edges.

issues.problem: SOURCE 1–3 distinguish slender pale curtain-wall framing from fine mesh balcony and ramp guards. CURRENT 16–17 uses prominent dark multi-rail barriers throughout, producing dense horizontal bands that obscure the glazing and ramp relationships.
issues.action: Replace the affected guard infill with fine mesh and reduce the visible rail/post sections to source proportions. Apply the source’s pale finish to these exposed members while preserving the separate curtain-wall grid.

keep: Concave transverse roof profile with unequal raised edges.
Alternating descent directions of the three ramp flights at the ramp end.
Rectangular concrete columns visible beneath the projecting upper enclosure.

issues.problem: CURRENT 15 and 19 show upper ramp landings projecting conspicuously beyond both sides of the glazed end elevation. In SOURCE 1’s frontal model photograph, those upper connections sit within the outer façade outline.
issues.action: Shorten and reposition the projecting upper landing ends locally, retaining the diagonal ramp runs. Connect each landing to its corresponding circulation deck without overlapping the façade framing.

issues.problem: CURRENT 25–26 show broadly continuous glazed enclosure lines and an undivided interior where SOURCE 7’s intermediate plans show repeated classroom partitions, stepped room fronts and a distinct open workspace. The source’s room-to-buffer-zone depth is consequently lost.
issues.action: Patch the affected intermediate enclosure bays with the source-shown partition returns and recessed entrances. Preserve verified structural columns; use a cutaway to check the partial floors before changing obscured slab geometry.

issues.problem: CURRENT 17 presents almost uninterrupted full-height glazing around the entrance level. SOURCE 3’s entrance has a substantial textured concrete header, while SOURCE 1–2 also show opaque lower enclosure bands and narrower glazing zones. These major wall-versus-glass distinctions are missing.
issues.action: Replace only the affected glazing portions with the observed concrete headers and opaque bands, matching their heights and positions against the entrance and adjoining source views.

keep: Concave transverse roof-edge silhouette with unequal raised ends.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 lower panel, SOURCE 5 section and SOURCE 7 middle plan show a substantial double-height workspace beside a partial intermediate floor. CURRENT 23 and 26 instead show closely stacked, continuous floor-and-beam levels, removing this defining interior void.
issues.action: Locally trim the intermediate slab and affected beams to the source-backed void boundary. Retain the adjacent occupied floor and supporting columns; connect the exposed floor edge and stair landing coherently.

issues.problem: SOURCE 1–2 show upper galleries terminating within the rectangular outer envelope, with slender mesh guards. CURRENT 15–16 and 19 show repeated balcony-like tabs projecting beyond both sides of the ramp elevation, plus open horizontal-bar guards that substantially change its outline and transparency.
issues.action: Shorten the unsupported gallery-end extensions to the source envelope, preserving the demonstrated ramp turning connections. Replace the visible gallery and ramp guard infill with the source’s fine mesh and slender framing; check each revised landing meets its ramp without overlap or a gap.

issues.problem: CURRENT 23 contains a diagonal chain of isolated stair treads, detached rectangular tread-like plates and a spiral flight whose upper passage is obstructed visually by continuous floor beams. SOURCE 4 shows a coherent spiral stair with a clear opening and connected landing.
issues.action: Remove stray tread pieces and locally resolve the spiral’s floor opening, beam clearance and landing connections. Retain only flights that form a continuous supported route between the intended levels.

keep: The recessed position of the upper hall inside the outer gallery perimeter.
The roof’s observed concave transverse profile.
The short-end arrangement of stacked diagonal ramps.

after_review.assessment: SOURCE panels show one elongated building: a retained concrete frame with a partial intermediate floor and double-height workspace, an added hall beneath a sagging timber roof, projecting glazed perimeter galleries, end ramps, and remote end stairs. Entrance views establish recessed glazing beneath grated galleries; interior views establish spiral stairs, circular floor openings and curved curtain enclosures. CURRENT captures the broad exterior arrangement, but its interior floor continuity, stair assembly and upper-hall enclosure remain inconsistent with those observations. The uncut section-direction views and roof-occluded plan cannot verify hidden openings or joints; no numerical dimensions are confirmed here.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 lower panel and SOURCE 5/8 sections show a substantial double-height workspace beside a partial intermediate floor. CURRENT 23/26 instead show repeated floor-and-beam layers continuing across the corresponding interior, suppressing that defining vertical space.
issues.action: Locally trim the intermediate slab and associated beams to the source-backed mezzanine boundary, retaining the surrounding concrete frame and connecting gallery.

issues.problem: CURRENT 23 shows the spiral stair disappearing into deep transverse beams, without a clearly resolved arrival opening. SOURCE 4 shows an unobstructed spiral flight connecting to the mezzanine. The current repeated brown horizontal plates also appear unsupported, unlike the source’s furnished workspace.
issues.action: Resolve the stair opening, beam clearance and landing connection locally. Give retained table plates their source-visible supports, or remove unsupported placeholder plates.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 upper panel shows large curved translucent curtain enclosures and a pale floor beneath a light timber ceiling. CURRENT 18 presents an undivided brown floor and substantially darker timber surfaces; the circular guards alone do not reproduce the observed spatial enclosure.
issues.action: Add the visible curved curtain tracks and suspended translucent curtains, preserving circulation around the circular openings; lighten the floor and timber finishes to match the source material zones.

keep: Concave transverse roof profile with unequal raised edges.
Recessed entrance glazing beneath the projecting gallery.
Alternating inclined ramp runs at the ramp end.

before_review.assessment: SOURCES 1–3 establish the ramp end, adjoining long elevation and recessed entrance through shared ramp, gallery and column landmarks. SOURCE 4 shows the curved timber ceiling above an open upper hall, plus a lower double-height workspace with a side mezzanine and spiral stair. SOURCES 5 and 8 show the stepped internal floor arrangement and buffer-envelope edges; SOURCE 6 distinguishes retained framing, timber addition and lightweight outer enclosure. SOURCE 7 shows repeated enclosed rooms, larger open spaces and end circulation. CURRENT captures the principal curved-roof silhouette, projecting glazed enclosure and ramp-end arrangement, but important internal divisions and clearances remain incorrect. Uncut views 19/22 and roof-occluded view 21 cannot verify the source sections or plans; exact dimensions and concealed connections remain uncertain.

issues.problem: SOURCE 7’s middle and lower plans show repeated enclosed rooms along one long side, with doors onto internal circulation. CURRENT 31–32 instead expose largely uninterrupted spaces between columns; the source-backed partition and doorway rhythm is missing.
issues.action: Add the observed room partitions and door openings locally on the corresponding levels, using the end stair/core and spiral stair to register the plans. Preserve the larger open hall areas.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4’s lower panel shows a clear double-height workspace, with its mezzanine concentrated along the side and the spiral stair rising through the opening. CURRENT 23 has substantial intermediate beams crossing this space and visually overlapping the stair’s upper flight, compromising both the open volume and stair clearance.
issues.action: Correct the local mezzanine opening and trim or terminate the crossing beams at its perimeter. Connect the spiral stair to the actual landing edge with a clear opening; retain framing outside this source-backed void.

issues.problem: SOURCE 5 and SOURCE 8 show a thin projecting buffer roof with an outward-tilted edge/ventilation assembly. CURRENT 33 presents a broad, uninterrupted horizontal cap terminating directly at the vertical curtain-wall head, omitting that articulated interface.
issues.action: Patch the perimeter cap profile and add the shown tilted edge assembly, with explicit connections to the glazing head. Preserve the central curved roof.

keep: Central roof’s concave transverse profile with unequal raised edges.
Alternating ramp flights at the ramp end.
Recessed lower entrance beneath the projecting upper enclosure.

after_review.assessment: SOURCE 1–3 establish the ramp end, adjoining long facade, glazed upper buffer and open ground-level frontage. SOURCE 4 shows the curved timber ceiling, translucent curtain enclosures and supported spiral stair; SOURCE 5–8 add sections, structural layers and three floor plans. CURRENT retains the recognizable ramp arrangement, recessed upper hall and sagging roof profile. The principal remaining differences concern the buffer eave, spiral-stair assembly and hall partitions. Uncut views and roof-obscured plans cannot establish fidelity of hidden floor openings; no confirmed dimensions were supplied.

issues.problem: SOURCE 5 and 8 show the buffer glazing terminating beneath a projecting, downward-sloping outer eave. CURRENT 33 and 37 terminate the nearly flat glazed roof at the outer facade frame, losing that distinct edge profile.
issues.action: Locally extend and slope the outer roof strip to reproduce the shown eave projection and its connection to the glazing; retain the existing inner roof framing.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 shows a spiral stair with a continuous central support and curved mesh guarding. CURRENT 23 shows exposed inner tread ends without a clearly continuous central support, and widely spaced vertical guard bars replace the source mesh.
issues.action: Patch the spiral assembly with a continuous central support connected to the treads and curved mesh infill. Check tread-to-landing connections through the floor openings.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4’s upper panel shows substantial translucent curtain enclosures on curved suspended tracks. CURRENT 18 presents an almost entirely open hall with circular guards, omitting these source-defining spatial divisions.
issues.action: Add the observed curved tracks and translucent hanging curtain surfaces in the corresponding hall regions, preserving the ceiling and circular opening guards.

keep: Concave transverse roof profile with unequal raised edges.
Alternating ramp flights at the ramp end.
Circular mesh guards around the small upper-hall openings.
The unobstructed recessed room doorway and gallery threshold visible in CURRENT 38.

before_review.assessment: Sources 1–2 show the ramp-facing short end and adjoining long elevation, with a recessed concrete frame, projecting glazed buffer, external ramps and curved timber roof. Source 3 shows the entrance and walkway underside; Source 4 shows upper and double-height lower interiors. Source 5 combines section and plan, Source 6 separates structural layers, Source 7 supplies three floor plans, and Source 8 supplies two sections. Recurring ramps, spiral stair and curved roof identify one building. CURRENT captures these principal elements, but the lower structural rhythm and interior assembly differ materially. Uncut CURRENT views cannot verify the sectional floor arrangement; no confirmed dimensions are supplied, and concealed joints remain uncertain.

issues.problem: CURRENT subdivides the lower long elevation into many repetitive narrow column-and-door units. The source plans and exterior model show fewer, wider structural bays, with openings arranged within that larger rhythm.
issues.action: Locally consolidate the extra lower columns and opening divisions to match the source bay positions; retain correctly placed perimeter walkways.

issues.problem: The source lower interior has a substantial double-height opening beside the spiral stair. CURRENT places deep horizontal members across this space and across the stair’s upper circulation zone, obscuring the intended open volume and suggesting unresolved clearance conflicts.
issues.action: Adjust the local floor opening and crossing members to reproduce the source double-height bay, ensuring the spiral stair connects to supported landings with clear headroom.

issues.problem: CURRENT contains isolated rectangular timber slabs at floor level and beside the spiral stair. Their visible ends lack supporting legs or continuous stair connections; the source shows supported furniture and a continuous spiral flight.
issues.action: Remove stray slabs or complete their source-supported furniture/stair connections. Resolve each exposed end rather than leaving floating pieces.

keep: Short-end roof edge curving downward toward the middle, with the right end higher.
Alternating external ramp flights across the short end.
Fine mesh infill within the upper circular opening guards.

after_review.assessment: SOURCE exterior perspectives, physical-model photographs and aerial drawing show one elongated building with a recessed lower frame, projecting glazed buffer galleries, end ramps and an elevated concave timber roof. Interior panels show a tall lower workspace with spiral circulation, exposed beams and shallow V bracing; the upper hall has circular guarded openings and translucent curved curtains. Plans and sections establish an asymmetric intermediate floor and substantial double-height space. CURRENT retains the recognizable exterior arrangement, but the lower interior appears substantially more obstructed, and its stair clearance remains unresolved. CURRENT uncut roof and elevation views do not verify the source floor voids or room layout; concealed regions remain uncertain. No numerical dimensions are confirmed by these images.

issues.problem: SOURCE shows a tall, open lower workspace beneath the upper floor, with intermediate accommodation concentrated to one side. CURRENT image 23 instead shows several horizontal beam/floor bands crossing the workspace and obscuring the spiral, suggesting that the source double-height opening is insufficient.
issues.action: Verify the opening against SOURCE sections 5 and 8 and plans 7; locally trim only floor infill and secondary members occupying that documented void. Preserve source-backed columns and perimeter framing.

issues.problem: CURRENT images 23 and 26 show a deep horizontal beam occupying the upper spiral flight/arrival clearance. The annular bridge demonstrates a landing connection, but does not establish an unobstructed route beneath this beam. SOURCE shows an open stair approach.
issues.action: Resolve the beam-to-flight conflict locally by coordinating the stair position, opening edge and landing elevation with the retained frame; show continuous clearance from the final treads onto the landing.

issues.problem: SOURCE interiors have pale timber soffits, light floors and visible shallow V-shaped under-beam bracing. CURRENT has dark floor and roof-soffit zones, while the lower interior lacks the prominent source bracing.
issues.action: Lighten the observed floor and timber-soffit materials and add the source-visible V bracing within the corresponding lower-hall bays after resolving the void and stair clearance.

keep: Concave roof edge with unequal end heights visible in the short-end comparison.
Alternating end-ramp arrangement.
Translucent curved curtain panels suspended from curved tracks in the upper hall.
Mesh guards around the small circular upper-floor openings.

before_review.assessment: SOURCE exterior perspectives, physical-model photographs and aerial drawing show one elongated building with a recessed lower frame, projecting glazed buffer galleries, end ramps and an elevated concave timber roof.
